exposure.statement: TDI for Cr(III) derived by the CONTAM Panel; dietary exposure well below.

Toddlers: chocolate (cocoa) products important in some surveys; in one survey (17 individuals) cocoa powder consumption made non-alcoholic beverages contribute up to 45% of Cr(III) exposure (possibly unrepresentative).
Other children: chocolate (cocoa) products 4-32% of Cr(III) exposure (median 12%); cocoa powder drove non-alcoholic beverages to 31% and 40% in two surveys.
Adolescents: chocolate (cocoa) products 4-30% (median 9%); non-alcoholic beverages 1-37% (median 8%) with important cocoa-powder (cocoa drink) contribution.
Elderly and very elderly: chocolate (cocoa) products lost relevance as a contributor.
High contribution of chocolate (cocoa) products is mainly due to high Cr(III) levels (group concentrations 500-1500 µg/kg) rather than high consumption.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary's toddler row puts 'up to 45% in one survey via cocoa beverages' under the chocolate products column; the primary attributes up to 45% to 'Non-alcoholic beverages' driven by cocoa powder consumption in a survey of only 17 individuals.
unresolved: Analyte is total chromium (assumed Cr(III)); no Cr(VI) data for cocoa.
Only means printed in Appendix E (no medians, P95 or ranges per food); per-food left-censoring not printed.
Sum of cocoa-product rows (239+10+4=253) plus 15 excluded = 268, consistent with Table 5, but cannot verify allocation of excluded samples.
